description: Multi-phase plans currently in flight. Each phase references roadmap item ids; the activePhase section breaks the current phase into concrete tasks with status. Survives conversation compactions — a fresh session can pick up by reading this file.

phases.title: Foundation
phases.notes: Schema, bus, episodic memory, agent base. Nothing alive yet — just the substrate everything else hangs off.

phases.title: First Voice
phases.notes: Cheshire Cat end-to-end. Talking to himself. Layered context composer + engagement policy + ADR writer come online here because the Cat is their first consumer.

phases.title: First Tension
phases.notes: Add the White Rabbit. Two voices, role tension, semantic + relational memory layers populated as the agents accumulate history. Compaction-as-behavior arrives because it has to.

phases.title: First Race
phases.notes: Dodo orchestrator + quiescence + conflict resolution + first showcase (/health endpoint). The system runs end-to-end on a trivial directive. Init CLI lands here so the showcase can run against a real target project.

phases.title: Full Cast
phases.notes: Bring the rest of the cast online with integration tests per agent. Per-character artifact handlers for the new speech act payloads. Synthetic-consensus guard goes here because it only matters once disagreement is real.

phases.title: Real Threads
phases.notes: The hard showcases — translation chat MVP, security recovery, multi-session persistence. Transcript annotation tooling lets us publish them. Token telemetry confirms the engagement_policy is paying for itself. Closed out 2026-05-08; substrate-convergence work in analyses 026-030 + the Geocities showcase landed the "Tweedles don't ship" bug class. P7 evals deferred behind P8 (operator interface) so the eval harness has a usable surface to run against.

phases.title: Observer API
phases.notes: HistoricalRunHandle reads any captured snapshot directory — parses run.log, reads the per-agent SQLite databases, loads the telemetry JSON, exposes summary() / meetings() / utterances() / per_agent_telemetry() / artifacts(). The replay-side surface that everything else in P8 sits on. Shipped 2026-05-07 alongside P8.2.

phases.title: TUI Inspector
phases.notes: Textual-based read-only TUI: snapshot library, run summary, meeting detail with body preview + speaker filter + utterance modal, artifact browser (global + meeting-scoped, attribution via bus not mtime), cast view, theme cycling, app-wide vim navigation. First public release — wonderland-ai 0.0.1 on PyPI 2026-05-08.

phases.title: Streaming + Mock Turtle
phases.notes: Foundation for live-watch UX. Extend RunHandle with stream_events() async iterator; HistoricalRunHandle defaults to yield-now (no behavior change for inspector); MockTurtleHandle replays a snapshot's events with compressed timing + dwell cap so we iterate live-watch UI against a free testbed. After P8.3 the TUI can subscribe to "events as they arrive" without caring whether the source is replay, mock, or eventually a real bus.

phases.title: Live-watch screen
phases.notes: New LiveRunScreen that consumes the streaming API — meeting cells fill in as events arrive, current speaker indicator, live cost ticker, drill-down into in-progress meetings shows partial transcripts. Iterated entirely against Mock Turtle replay so zero API spend during UX iteration. The screen that turns Wonderland from "things happen and you read transcripts later" into "things happen and you watch them happen."

phases.title: Directive issuing + LiveRunHandle
phases.notes: NewRunScreen — directive textarea, workflow picker (TDD/canonical/smoke), project-root picker. LiveRunHandle wraps a real Runner+Caucus, emits via the same streaming API as MockTurtleHandle so the live-watch screen consumes both interchangeably. The leap from "replay testbed" to "actually launches a real run." First end-to-end test: directive → live watch → artifacts → done.

phases.title: New-project spinup (the rabbit hole)
phases.notes: Three entry paths converging on a single project-context capture: greenfield (skeleton picker + scaffold), existing-Wonderland (already covered by P8.5's project picker), adopt-existing (wonderland init + stack-detection routine that pre-fills the context form from manifest files). Persists .wonderland/project-context.md in a forward-compatible shape so future workflow-context injection has one input format to read. The on-ramp that turns "pip install" into "team's ready to start."

phases.title: First-use polish
phases.notes: Welcome/home screen (new run / browse snapshots / cast / configure), error states (missing API key, no project root, run failure), abort flow (clean shutdown of running threads), quiescence indicator (M5's long pauses need "still working, just thinking"), README + SHOWCASE updates with the TUI flow. The rough-edges sweep that closes the gap between "works for the developer" and "works for someone who just installed it."

phases.title: Evals
phases.notes: Generic-baseline vs Wonderland comparison. The compounding-curve plot is the legibility-of-value mitigation from §11. Without this the philosophy stays assertion.

phases.title: Meeting turns: phases + priority + rotations
phases.notes: Per analysis 033 (analyses/033-meeting-as-mtg-turn.md): lift phases + priority rotation + turns-as-budget from MtG into the meeting engine; skip the stack. Sequenced as a substrate phase that alternates with P8's interface track per the back-and-forth-stays-fresh rhythm. Engine work is bigger than P8's per-task shape and benefits from its own phase boundary. Engine + workflow schema + observer events are P1 (load-bearing); rotation counter + failure-mode detectors are P2 (instrumentation that lands once the structure exists).

phases.title: Two-Headed Giant: team windows
phases.notes: Per the live r35-tdd-serial-phased observation: strict-serial priority within a rotation imposes ~N× cast size wall-clock cost on constitutionally-paired agents (Tweedledee/Tweedledum, Alice/Hatter) who in legacy mode would have deliberated concurrently. Phase 9.5 generalizes phases by adding team_groupings: list[list[str]] per phase. A team window opens concurrently for all team members via asyncio.gather; structural cap preserved (rotation budget × team count = bounded deliberations); §VIII observability preserved (per-agent WindowOutcome unchanged). Maps onto MtG's Two-Headed Giant format — paired players take their team turn together. The natural design follow-up to P9; lands once analysis 034 quantifies the wall-clock penalty of the strict-serial baseline.

phases.title: Cost recovery: tool-call surfacing + diff-based writes
phases.notes: Per analyses 032 + 035: Tweedles are 78.8% of total run cost, with ~13-15 calls per deliberation reflecting heavy write_file → run_tests → write_file tool loops. Two batched fixes: (1) surface tool calls on the bus event log so post-run analysis can quantify exactly which tool calls drive cost (currently inferred via per-agent telemetry); (2) diff-based write tool that lets agents send deltas instead of full file contents, with analysis 032 estimating ~3.5× cost compression on iterative file authoring. Sequencing: surface first so we can measure baseline tool-call distribution; then diff tool with measurements to verify the predicted compression. After both ship, second pass to identify other easy cost/clock wins from whatever the surfaced data reveals.

activePhase.title: Cost recovery: tool-call surfacing + diff-based writes
activePhase.goal: Reduce Tweedle cost (the 78.8% cost-driver per analysis 035) via two complementary substrate additions: tool-call event surfacing for measurement; diff-based file editing for token compression. Together they should cut a phased-run-equivalent of r36 from ~$8.85 toward ~$6 without losing output quality. The expected mechanism (per analysis 032's estimate): write_file traffic in M5's iterate-red-green loop sends the full file on each iteration; with diff-based writes, Tweedles send 30-50 lines per iteration instead of 250-400, cutting input tokens roughly 3-4× on the bulk of M5's calls.
activePhase.sequencing: Tool-call surfacing first (T66) — without it we can't measure baseline write_file/read_file/run_tests distribution and can't validate the diff tool's claimed compression. Then diff-based write tool (T67) — str_replace + insert primitives wrapping the existing write_file path, with the LLM choosing between full-write and patch on a per-call basis. Then T68: re-run pomodoro through tdd-serial-phased and A/B vs r36 — same workflow, same directive, headline metric is total cost (target: 25-35% reduction) and per-Tweedle calls/deliberation ratio (target: drop from ~14 to ~10 as patch-write replaces full-write in the tool loop).

tasks.title: Surface tool calls on the bus event log
tasks.details: Per roadmap 33e29f5c: extend the event log so each tool invocation (write_file / read_file / run_tests / list_files / grep) emits an event observable by post-run analysis. Surfacing should include tool name, arguments (path, query terms), input/output token counts when available, and the deliberation context (which agent's window, which phase). Goal: enable cost-attribution by tool, so future analyses can answer 'what fraction of Tweedle cost is write_file?' directly rather than inferring from per-agent telemetry. Implementation likely lives at the tools layer (src/wonderland/tools.py) with a callback registered by the runner; events flow into the existing telemetry.json and a new tool-calls.jsonl on disk.
tasks.resolution: Tool-call observability shipped. ToolCallEvent dataclass + serialize/deserialize helpers + jsonl_tool_call_writer factory + read_tool_calls reader (mirrors the phase-events.jsonl pattern from T58d). Tools.__init__ accepts optional on_tool_call: ToolCallWriter callback. Tools.execute wraps the dispatch with timing capture (start/elapsed_ms via time.monotonic), result-size measurement (UTF-8 byte length), error capture (ToolError or general Exception), and best-effort writer invocation in finally so observability never masks the underlying tool result. Args summarization keeps small fields verbatim (path, pattern) and replaces large content blobs with byte-count entries (write_file's content arg becomes content_bytes — keeps JSONL small while capturing the cost of resending the whole file). agent_id propagated from agent.deliberate's tool loop via self.identity.name. Runner installs a default writer at <project_root>/.wonderland/tool-calls.jsonl. 6 new tests cover callback firing per-dispatch, large-content summarization, error capture, writer-failure isolation, JSONL round-trip, missing-file empty-list path. Full suite: 1516 pass.

tasks.title: Diff-based write tool: str_replace + insert
tasks.details: Per roadmap 0858a936 + analysis 032's ~3.5× compression estimate. Add tool methods: str_replace(path, old, new) and insert(path, line_number, content). LLM chooses per-call between full write_file and patch operations. Validation: each str_replace requires exact match for old; inserts require valid line numbers. Constitutional update for Tweedles: hint at 'prefer str_replace for incremental changes; use write_file only for new files or wholesale rewrites.' Implementation in src/wonderland/tools.py; tests cover round-trip patch application + edge cases (no match, ambiguous match, line-number bounds).
tasks.resolution: Diff-based write tools shipped. Tools.str_replace(path, old, new): exactly-one-match validation (ToolError on 0 or N>1 matches), empty-old rejection (use insert instead), deletion via empty-new. Tools.insert(path, line_number, content): 1-indexed line numbers (0 prepends), bounds-checked, auto-trailing-newline so insertions don't fuse with following lines. Both stash post-patch file size in self._last_op_metadata for the observability hook to read; ToolCallEvent gains file_size_after_bytes field — comparison baseline for 'bytes saved vs hypothetical full write' aggregation in T68's analysis. Tool-use schema descriptions guide the LLM to prefer str_replace/insert for incremental edits and reserve write_file for new files / wholesale rewrites — constitutional update deferred until T68 reveals whether the schema-level hint is enough. 16 new tests cover unique-match application, ambiguous-match rejection, deletion via empty new, missing-file errors, dispatch round-trip, insert prepend / mid-file / append, out-of-bounds rejection, auto-newline behavior, file_size_after_bytes accuracy on both ops + None for write_file. Full suite: 1532 pass.

tasks.title: Re-run + cost A/B + analysis 036
tasks.details: After T66 + T67 ship, re-run pomodoro through tdd-serial-phased. A/B vs r36 (the team-windows baseline). Headline metric: total cost (predict 25-35% reduction = ~$6 not $8.85). Secondary: per-Tweedle calls/deliberation ratio (predict ~10 not ~14). Tool-call surfacing data lets analysis 036 quantify the actual diff-tool adoption rate and per-call token savings. If cost reduction matches prediction, the cost-recovery phase closes; if not, the surfaced tool-call data tells us where the next intervention should target.

tasks.title: Agent-to-user question affordance: ask_user tool + TUI modal
tasks.details: Per roadmap 9aae11bc and the r37/r38 architectural-ambiguity pattern (server-client vs client-only seam tripped Tweedles in r37, hitting Alice in r38). Substrate: new ask_user(question, options=[]) tool surfaced in tool_definitions; agent.deliberate's tool loop catches it specially (bypasses Tools.execute) and awaits an injected async handler. TUI: AskUserModal ModalScreen with question + RadioSet for options + free-text Input + Submit/Skip. LiveRunHandle wires the handler on each agent during runner setup; modal resolves a Future the agent awaits. Default handler (when no UI attached): returns 'ask_user not available; proceed with best judgment' as tool_output, so headless runs degrade gracefully. Tests cover schema present, agent dispatch, modal flow, default fallback.
tasks.resolution: Agent-to-user question affordance shipped via the utterance pattern (not tool call — chosen because it makes the question + answer first-class bus artifacts visible to other agents). OPERATOR_NAME / OPERATOR_CONSTITUTION_VERSION constants + operator_identity() factory + is_question_to_operator() helper in utterance.py. Runner gains set_user_question_handler + _watch_user_questions background task that subscribes to the bus, detects QUESTION-to-operator utterances, calls the registered handler, and publishes OBSERVATION-from-operator with parent_id back-reference (so subsequent agents see both Q and A in their compose_context). Runner also gains wait_for_question_answer with answered-questions cache + pending-future registry to handle the race between phase orchestrator and watcher. Phase orchestrator awaits the operator reply before opening the next window when an agent's act was a QUESTION-to-operator. LiveRunHandle gains set_user_question_handler that wires through to the runner during stream_events setup. AskUserModal ModalScreen shows the question + free-text input + Submit/Skip buttons, dismisses with reply text or None on skip. LiveRunScreen wires _handle_user_question that pushes the modal and bridges the dismiss callback into the awaiting coroutine via asyncio.Future. Constitutional hint added in primer.py — agents can address the operator with a QUESTION when the team can't resolve internally; sparingly, not as a fallback for 'I don't know what to write'. 4 new utterance tests + 2 phase orchestrator tests covering the operator-question path and the no-trigger-on-non-operator-questions baseline. Full suite: 1538 pass.
